picks.title: Google's new SynthID website can identify AI-generated media
picks.excerpt: Google launched a public SynthID website that lets anyone check whether images, video or audio (including Lyria music) carry Google's AI watermark.
picks.rationale: New public tool: anyone can now upload audio and check for Google's AI watermark, including Lyria-generated music. Useful for labels, curators and artists trying to verify a track's origin.

picks.title: BIFF opening-ceremony AI entrance song: director Min Kyu-dong explains the intent
picks.excerpt: 제31회 부산국제영화제 개막식에서 게스트 이름을 가사에 넣은 AI 입장곡이 화제·논란이 된 가운데, 개막식을 총지휘한 민규동 감독이 기획 의도를 밝혔다.
picks.rationale: A concrete Korean case: personalised AI-generated entrance songs were used at a major public ceremony, and the director explains the controversy. Gives the brief a local, applied angle.

picks.title: Smorph: playable diffusion-based sound morphing for musical sound design
picks.excerpt: Smorph makes diffusion-based sound morphing playable for musical sound design by disentangling temporal structure from timbre transitions.
picks.rationale: Producer-facing research: separating temporal structure from timbre makes generative sound morphing playable as an instrument rather than only renderable offline.

picks.title: Ghost in the Encoder: artist identity is decodable inside lyrics-to-song generation models
picks.excerpt: 'Ghost in the Encoder' shows artist identity is decodable from internal representations of lyrics-to-song generation models, probing how they imitate artists or regurgitate songs.
picks.rationale: New evidence for the imitation and regurgitation debate: artist identity can be read out of song-generation models' internal representations, which bears directly on the ongoing label-versus-Suno litigation.
